run.title: Build release-readiness HTTP service
run.body: Build a complete Python standard-library release-readiness HTTP service in app.py. This is an original useful tool for deciding whether an observed release has had enough soak time. CLI: python app.py --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8767. RELEASE_SHA environment variable is required and must be a full 40-character lowercase hex git SHA; fail startup clearly if absent/invalid. GET /health returns JSON {status: "ok", revision: RELEASE_SHA}. GET /readiness?deployed_at=<ISO8601 with explicit timezone>&observation_seconds=<nonnegative integer> returns JSON with ready boolean, elapsed_seconds nonnegative, remaining_seconds nonnegative and revision. Future deployment timestamps are not ready; readiness becomes true exactly when elapsed >= observation duration. Invalid/missing timestamps, timezone-naive timestamps, negative/noninteger observation durations return HTTP400 JSON error. Unknown path returns404 JSON. Use an importable pure calculation function accepting an explicit timezone-aware now datetime for deterministic tests; HTTP handler uses current UTC time. Include meaningful unittest tests in tests/test_app.py for readiness boundary, future timestamps, timezone offsets, invalid input, health revision and HTTP routes using temporary ephemeral test ports. No third-party dependencies. README documents how to run and sample requests. Scope only app.py, tests/test_app.py, README.md. Do not access the network or shell; return the requested JSON proposals. Avoid actual clock sleeps in tests.

acceptance: Starting `python app.py --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8767` requires `RELEASE_SHA` to be present and exactly a 40-character lowercase hexadecimal SHA; absent or invalid values fail startup with a clear error.
`GET /health` returns HTTP 200 JSON containing `{"status":"ok","revision":RELEASE_SHA}`.

`GET /readiness?deployed_at=<timezone-aware ISO8601>&observation_seconds=<nonnegative integer>` returns HTTP 200 JSON with `ready`, nonnegative `elapsed_seconds`, nonnegative `remaining_seconds`, and `revision`.
Readiness is false for future deployment timestamps and becomes true exactly when elapsed seconds are greater than or equal to `observation_seconds`.
Missing, invalid, or timezone-naive `deployed_at` values and missing, negative, or noninteger `observation_seconds` values return HTTP 400 JSON error responses.
Unknown routes return HTTP 404 JSON error responses.
A pure importable readiness calculation function accepts explicit timezone-aware `now` datetime values for deterministic unit tests.
HTTP readiness uses the current UTC time without test sleeps.
`python -m unittest discover -s tests -v` passes using only the Python standard library.
README documents startup requirements, run command, endpoints, and sample requests.
spec.design: Use `http.server.ThreadingHTTPServer` and `BaseHTTPRequestHandler` from the standard library. `app.py` will expose importable helpers such as `validate_release_sha`, `parse_deployed_at`, `parse_observation_seconds`, and `calculate_readiness(deployed_at, observation_seconds, now, revision)` so unit tests can exercise deterministic behavior without depending on wall-clock time. The HTTP handler will parse `urlparse(self.path)`, dispatch only `/health` and `/readiness`, serialize all responses as JSON, and return JSON errors for 400/404 cases. For ISO8601 parsing, normalize a trailing `Z` to `+00:00` before `datetime.fromisoformat`, then require `tzinfo` and a valid UTC offset. Elapsed seconds will be computed from `now - deployed_at` after timezone normalization, floored to integer seconds, clamped at zero for future deployments, and remaining seconds computed as `max(0, observation_seconds - elapsed_seconds)`. Tests will start the HTTP server in-process on port 0 with an injected revision and stop it cleanly, avoiding shell, network beyond localhost, and sleeps. Alternative frameworks are unnecessary and out of scope because only the standard library is allowed.
spec.rollback: Revert changes to `app.py`, `tests/test_app.py`, and `README.md`. If only documentation or tests need rollback, restore the previous README contents and remove the new test file while leaving no generated artifacts.
steps: Create `app.py` with RELEASE_SHA validation, pure readiness calculation, HTTP request handler, JSON response helpers, route parsing, and argparse-based server startup.
Implement strict parsing for full lowercase 40-character SHA, timezone-aware ISO8601 datetimes including `Z`, and nonnegative integer observation durations.
Ensure readiness calculation clamps elapsed and remaining seconds to nonnegative values and evaluates ready as `elapsed >= observation_seconds`.

Add `tests/test_app.py` covering pure calculation boundary behavior, future timestamps, timezone offset handling, invalid query inputs, health response revision, readiness route behavior, unknown route 404, and RELEASE_SHA validation/server setup using ephemeral localhost ports.
Update `README.md` with overview, required environment variable, command-line usage, endpoint descriptions, example curl requests, and test command.
Keep implementation limited to `app.py`, `tests/test_app.py`, and `README.md`; use no third-party dependencies and no real sleep-based tests.
spec.summary: Plan to implement a Python standard-library release-readiness HTTP service with deterministic readiness calculation, JSON HTTP endpoints, validation, tests, and README usage documentation.
